why: Node step 558 (owner 2026-10-21): what this memory element CAN run on a schedule — its backup events (handlers written in advance, build process). The person's schedule is NOT here: it is data, `data/cron.json` (outside git). The core draws events + schedule as the calendar under «Backup → Cron events»; the element's server checks the clock once a minute (lib/cron/). A missed run (computer off) is not caught up. Skill: backup-schedule. Never published in /.well-known/agent-card.json. Node step 636: the built-in `agent-task` wakes only this element's own agent; words for the person go through the core's main agent. Node step 636-8: a reminder for the person is `node-notice` — the core's notice door puts the words into the main chat, no model; `agent-task` only for work that needs the agent at that time.

events.name: Notice in the main chat
events.description: Sends the schedule's own text (field «message») into the node's main chat through the core's notice door: «⏰ Reminder · <this element>» and the words as a quote — no model, no agent woken (node step 636-8). Any reminder for the person is this event.

events.name: Wake this element's agent
events.description: Wakes this element's own agent with the schedule's own text (field «message») for work that needs it at that time — a check, a copy, a report; the session costs the subscription. Words for the person are not this event: they are `node-notice`. No other agent is reached (node step 636).

events.name: Message in Telegram
events.description: Sends the schedule's own text (field «message») to this element's Telegram bot — for example, «the copy is done».
